# Owned enum token and default fixture

Static factories retain one method-owned E extends Enum<E> across a Class<E>
token, optional direct default input and E result beside an independent Object
context. Source and SDK-provider profiles compile every recovered unit and
preserve original entries, fields, flags, metadata and Exceptions.
Frozen direct, separately compiled, reflection and MethodHandle callers run
144 fresh JVM cases twice. They check exact token/value/default/result identity,
nulls, aliases, mismatched tokens and enum classes, mutations, opaque results
and exact callback and late cast/null failures. Six wrong programs and six
Code-preserving Signature controls guard the recursive bound and erasures.
Only owned fixture and standard SDK enum code executes. Use JDK 25 for the
runner; originals use release 8 and recovery uses its reported Java release.

The string-context variants retain a closed String input beside the invariant
`Class<E>` token and the same recursive `E` default/result formal. Static and
instance providers each run as source or SDK declarations. The immutable
instance observer adds a future override and a null provider: virtual dispatch
must occur once, while null must fail before provider effects. All original
metadata, Code/access roles, late result casts and exact failures remain checked;
no token contents or provider result is predicted.
